title: Per-model Performance Mosaic: Hybrid Strips & Microtrend Charts
creator: Anika Rao
description: Design a compact, scannable per-model performance view that blends three visual idioms: a horizontal 'strip' lane for latency percentiles, a vertical microtrend spark area for token throughput, and a compact cost-per-token heat ribbon. The goal is a single-glance mosaic for SREs/engineers and PMs to evaluate model health across routes and quickly pivot to deeper traces. This ticket covers high-fidelity specs for the three chart components, interaction patterns for time-range linking, lightweight annotations for regression flags, and a responsive layout that fits inside existing route-detail panels.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity Figma screens for desktop (1280–1920) and a condensed mobile/tablet variant
Chart spec doc including data schema, aggregation windows, percentile lines, marker behavior, and color tokens
Interaction flows: hover tooltips, click-to-open microtrace, time-range sync across mosaic tiles, and export CSV action
Engineering-ready notes: recommended back-end aggregations (1s, 10s, 1m), sample API responses, and suggested defaults for smoothing and sampling
Design review sign-off from PM (Riley Park) and Eng lead (Sanjay Iyer) with follow-up list addressed
updates: 2026-03-10: Initial brief and low-fi sketch uploaded. Focus: reduce vertical real estate while preserving percentile detail.

2026-03-11: Added alternative layout that prioritizes token throughput when cost-sensitivity label is present. Trade-off note: throughput-first reduces immediate latency visibility but surfaces cost anomalies.

2026-03-12: Engineering sync — Sanjay recommends pre-aggregated percentile endpoints (p50/p90/p99) and a separate raw-sample stream for microtrace drilldowns. Agreed on 1s sample for microtrend, 10s and 1m for dashboard rollups.
2026-03-13: Design review held. PM feedback: include a lightweight anomaly flag and configurable metric pins per route. Action items created for pinning UX and annotation legend.
2026-03-13: Updated Figma with hover states, keyboard focus order, and accessible color variants (WCAG AA aim).
reviews: Riley Park (PM) — +1 on layout; requested clearer CTA to open rollout compare and suggested an A/B strip overlay for rollout comparators.
Sanjay Iyer (Eng) — raised concern about data cardinality for sub-route breakdowns; asked for guidance on default sampling windows and when to fall back to coarse aggregates.
Lena Ortiz (SRE) — asked for a 'last incident' marker, and that time-range sync should persist across console pages when a route is pinned.
Design critique notes — consider micro-interactions for toggling percentile bands to aid visual clarity for small-screen monitors.
decisions: Use hybrid visualization: horizontal percentile strip + inline microtrend spark + cost ribbon; this preserves percentile fidelity while surfacing token throughput patterns.
Default aggregation windows: p50/p90/p99 at 10s rollup, microtrend at 1s sample (with a configurable sampling knob in the Console settings).
Anomaly flagging: server-side anomaly score prop surfaced as a small badge; tooltip includes incident link if available.
next_steps: Address review action items: add rollout-compare CTA, implement pinning UX copy, and surface 'last incident' marker in designs.
Produce an engineering handoff doc with JSON schema examples for chart payloads and suggested PromQL snippets for demo clusters.
Schedule a follow-up sign-off meeting with SRE and Eng (target 2026-03-20).
